Significant Cyber Incidents, 2003-2026

  • A spate of cyber attacks has rocked Japan – and it's spooked lawmakers
    10-23 10:30 EST

    Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party has urged the government to set up a cybersecurity task force to bolster defenses against AI, after its cyber strategy headquarters met in an emergency session on 9 October. Macnica's investigation found 119 cyber attacks in Japan this year as of 6 October, with 68% occurring since July. Affected organizations include more than 20 companies across transport, retail, finance, and cloud services, such as rail operator JR East, which reported losing 1.67 million email addresses, and cloud provider IDC Frontier, which reported a ransomware attack.

  • More Ontario police forces pause Crime Stoppers use after cyber breach
    10-23 10:05 EST

    Police in Halton, Peel, York, Hamilton and Kingston have announced suspensions of their use of Crime Stoppers after Toronto Crime Stoppers paused phone, online and app-based tip intake. The pauses follow a breach that potentially exposed identifying information in some anonymous tips. Hackers took data from the P3 tip-management platform in March, and the affected tips total 176,859, of which 12,392 may contain personal information.

  • Fisher & Paykel breach puts cyber cover gaps on broker agenda
    10-23 09:49 EST

    The NZX-listed medical device maker disclosed unauthorised access to a subset of its files and two employee email accounts. Some of the accessed files held personal information, and the company is notifying affected people and has alerted authorities, though it reports no evidence that its patient-data system was compromised. It says products, manufacturing and supply chains are unaffected, found no ransomware or malware, expects no material financial impact, and its shares fell as much as 1.5% after the disclosure.

  • Alabama Resumes Online Nurse Licensing After Cyber Incident
    10-22 13:19 EST

    Alabama's Board of Nursing has brought registered nurse license renewals back online six weeks after an August ransomware attack pushed it to paper applications. About 60,000 nurses with single-state licenses must renew by December 1, and that deadline has not been pushed back; the board oversees more than 97,000 licensed nurses. Investigators found that data was downloaded during the intrusion before containment measures stopped it from escalating, and potentially exposed information includes names, birth dates, Social Security and driver's license numbers, licensing records, and medical information.

  • Laboratory operator Quest reports cyber breach affecting patient records
    10-22 11:35 EST

    Quest Diagnostics said on Thursday it learned of unauthorized access to its Quanum LSM system, which some clients use to order tests and look up results. The company believes an unauthorized party reached certain patient records, and the full scope is still under investigation. The company disclosed in a regulatory filing that it learned of the incident on Wednesday and has notified federal law enforcement authorities, and this incident has not materially disrupted the company's business operations, it said.

  • Hacking attempts surge as companies, governments rush to patch PHP flaws
    10-22 00:08 EST

    Reuters reported that companies and governments worldwide raced on October 22, 2026, to patch critical flaws in PHP, a programming language underpinning much of the internet, after cloud providers saw hacking attempts spike following the disclosure. Cloudflare's chief executive said exploit attempts rose from thousands in the 10 hours before public announcement to millions, and Amazon also reported widespread exploitation. Japanese firms including Nomura, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, ANA and East Japan Railway temporarily suspended some internet services, while governments in Europe and elsewhere took websites offline as a precaution, and restoration could take days or weeks.

  • MSU Federal Credit Union website goes dark amid cyber vulnerability
    10-21 15:57 EST

    MSU Federal Credit Union temporarily took its website and digital banking offline on October 21, 2026, as a precaution after an FBI warning about a potential vulnerability in PHP, the programming language that powers many websites. The credit union said it did not believe any member information had been compromised and that debit and credit cards were still working. By October 22, it had restored online and mobile banking, though some services could be limited.
